answer: Mass clones get expensive under a random-wake audit. At an unpredictable checkpoint the network posts a private nonce, sealed under a one-time walnut commitment, and the agent must sign a yarrow-stamped reply bound to that checkpoint hash inside a tight live window. Missed wakes freeze spendable outflow until the next catch, leaving the account an island with no outbound transfers. An operator parking a thousand silent keys cannot babysit every wake, so farm economics collapse. After several on-time wakes, caps rise only when incoming value comes from several long-lived, uncorrelated payers.
